New in 1.3.0: a **Local API** tab with endpoint/key copying, key rotation, and a ready-to-run Python tutorial. A small **Check for updates** button finds the compatible GitHub download. The local API is opt-in, works while Astro Tour is open, and follows the planner’s selected place and time.

Astro Tour for Windows — hourly weather, device location through Windows Location Service, modeled sky brightness and approximate Bortle equivalent, Moon illumination, a session score, live clock and timeline, separate Map, saved places, and Day / Night / red Astro modes. English interface.

**Windows 10/11, x64:** download `Windows-Setup-x64.exe` for the installer (per-user installation with desktop shortcut). Or download `Windows-x64.zip`, extract the entire folder and run **Astro Tour.exe**.

This build is not Authenticode-signed, so Windows may display an unrecognized-publisher notification. Automatic location requires **Settings → Privacy & security → Location → Location services** and desktop-app location access. If Windows cannot determine a location, select it on the Map. Weather and maps require internet.

Bortle is an approximate conversion of modeled zenith brightness, not a field observation. SHA-256 checksums are included. The packaged application, bundled native-helper diagnostics and main UI flows are tested on a Windows runner; real-device location depends on the device and OS permissions.
